impact_assessment.why: Recorded improvement backlog from the verification passes: output is limited to table/json, grouping by directory requires external scripting, and files with no commit history are invisible in the report even though their complexity makes them risk material
impact_assessment.benefits: CSV gives scriptable spreadsheet-compatible output; dir grouping answers 'which area churns' directly; --all surfaces new uncommitted files whose complexity is invisible today
impact_assessment.risks: contract: --format gains a choice and two new flags, all additive; CSV score column follows the 3-decimal display precision (WYSIWYG) while JSON keeps stored precision; --all can produce large tables (bounded by --top); grouping semantics: top-level files group as '.', aggregation is additive sums before ranking
impact_assessment.mitigation: each feature is one milestone with failing-first tests; reuse rank_hotspots for grouped scoring so tie-breaking and drop rules stay single-sourced; ls-files --exclude-standard respects .gitignore; README updated same commit per milestone
